title: How to use LEFT, RIGHT and MID in Excel
description: Learn how to extract text in Excel using LEFT, RIGHT, and MID, with clear examples and a link to hands-on practice.

args.name: text
args.text: The text string or cell reference containing the characters you want to extract.

args.name: num_chars
args.text: The number of characters to extract. Defaults to 1 if omitted in LEFT and RIGHT. Required in MID.

args.name: start_num
args.text: The position of the first character to extract in MID, starting at 1 for the first character.

sections.heading: Extract from the start with LEFT
sections.text: **LEFT** pulls characters from the beginning of a text string. Give it a cell reference and the number of characters you want. If you omit the character count, Excel returns just the first character.

sections.heading: Extract from the end with RIGHT
sections.text: **RIGHT** pulls characters from the end of a text string. Give it a cell reference and how many characters to return from the right side. If you omit the count, it returns only the last character.

sections.heading: Extract from the middle with MID
sections.text: **MID** returns a specific number of characters from anywhere inside a text string. You specify the text, the position where extraction starts, and how many characters to take. Unlike `LEFT` and `RIGHT`, the length is required.

sections.heading: Common mistake: numbers returned as text
sections.text: Text functions always return text strings, even when the characters look like numbers. If you extract digits like `940`, formulas like `SUM` will ignore that cell. Remember also that Excel uses 1-based indexing, so the first character is always 1, not 0. To use extracted digits in calculations, wrap your formula in `VALUE`, such as `=VALUE(RIGHT(A2, 3))`.
